settings.name_in_paper: Survival bandit problem (S-MAB), multinomial arms on {-1,0,1}
unmapped: Reward distributions are multinomial with support {-1,0,1}
Ruin constraint: the procedure stops at the first round where B + cumulative reward <= 0 (initial budget B)
Objectives are probability of ruin and asymptotic relative regret rate (Pareto optimality), not standard regret
settings.definition_quote: An agent starts with a budget $B_0 = B$. Then, at every round $t\in \{1, \dots, T\}$ while the agent's budget satisfies $B_{t-1}>0$, the agent selects an arm $\pi_t \in [K]$; the agent observes a reward $X_t^{\pi_t}$ drawn from $F_{\pi_t}$; the agent updates its budget as $B_t := B_{t-1} + X_t^{\pi_t}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Survival bandit problem (S-MAB), arm distributions bounded in [-1,1]
unmapped: Ruin constraint: the procedure stops at the first round where B + cumulative reward <= 0 (initial budget B)
Objectives are probability of ruin and asymptotic relative regret rate (Pareto optimality)
settings.definition_quote: Let $\mathcal{F}_{[-1,1]}$ be the set of distributions bounded in $[-1, 1]$ which are not positive or zero.

conditions: Pareto-type statement: if P_F(ruin) is below the bound for some F, it is strictly above it for another F

source.label: non_asymptotic_lower_bound_theorem
source.quote: Let $(\alpha_k)_{k\in [K]}$ be such that for any $k, \ \alpha_k > 0$ and $\sum_{k=1}^K \alpha_k = 1$. For any policy $\pi$, \inf_{F} \{P_{F}(\tau(B, \pi)<\infty) - \exp(- B\sum_{k=1}^K \alpha_k \gamma(F_k))\} < 0 \implies \sup_{F} \{...\} >0.

results.notes: Pareto-type lower bound on the probability of ruin P(tau(B,pi)<infinity), not a regret bound.

symbols.B_k: budget share of arm k, positive integers summing to B

tuning: budget shares B_1,...,B_K with sum B

source.label: exploit_proba_ruin_proposition
source.quote: Given some positive integers $B_1, \dots, B_K$ such that $B_1 + \dots + B_K = B$, all the policies in EXPLOIT$(B_1, \dots, B_K)$ achieve the same probability of ruin, given by p^{EX}(B_1,...,B_K) = \prod_{k=1}^K P_{F_k}(\tau(B_k, k)<\infty) = \exp(- \sum_{k=1}^K B_k \gamma(F_k)).

results.notes: Probability of ruin (equality), matching Theorem 10; applies to EXPLOIT-UCB as well.

symbols.p_EX: probability of ruin of EXPLOIT with near-equal budget shares

source.label: proba_survival_exploit_dbl
source.quote: Given $n\geq 1$, the probability of ruin of EXPLOIT-UCB-DOUBLE is bounded as follows: P(\tau(B, \pi^n) < \infty) \leq p^{\mathrm{EX}} + \frac{(p^{\mathrm{EX}})^{nB}}{1 - (p^{\mathrm{EX}})^{nB}} = p^{\mathrm{EX}} + o(1) if n -> infinity.

results.notes: Bound on the probability of ruin. Proposition 30 restates it for rewards in [-1,1].

symbols.o_T: a term o(T): mu_star*T minus the expected reward given no ruin is o(T)

tuning: n -> infinity with T and n = o(T^{1/4})

source.label: reward_exploit_dbl
source.quote: Let $n$ be such that $n\xrightarrow{T\to+\infty} +\infty$ and that $n = o(T^{1/4})$. Then, the reward given no ruin of EXPLOIT-UCB-DOUBLE with input parameter $n$ is bounded from below by \E[\sum_{t=1}^T X_t^{\pi^n_t} \1_{\tau(B, \pi^n)\geq t-1} | \tau(B, \pi^n) \geq T] \geq \max_{k\in [K]} \mu_k T + o(T).

results.notes: Sublinear regret conditional on no ruin; expressed as an o(T) gap with no explicit rate. n depends on T, so the horizon is known.

conditions: Pareto-type: holds whenever sup_F Reg(pi^n||pi') > 0, for any competing sequence of policies pi'

source.label: fake_teaser_theorem
source.quote: For any sequence of policies $\pi'$, the anytime policy EXPLOIT-UCB-DOUBLE with input parameter $n$ satisfies \sup_{F} \Reg(\pi^n\|\pi') > 0 \implies \inf_F \Reg(\pi^n\|\pi') < \frac{(p^{\mathrm{EX}})^{nB}}{1 - (p^{\mathrm{EX}})^{nB}}\max_{k\in [K]} \mu_k.

results.notes: The relative regret rate is limsup (Rew diff)/T, so the bound is multiplied by T. It is an 'almost Pareto-optimal' statement, not a standard regret bound. Theorem 23 (n = log T gives exact regret-wise Pareto optimality) is a qualitative statement and is not recorded as a separate bound. Proposition 30 restates this for [-1,1] rewards.

conditions: hard instances are Bernoulli arms on {-1,1}
results.notes: A positive relative regret rate means some competitor gains Omega(T) reward. The constant depends on the instance and is not explicit.

conditions: Pareto-type statement over F in F_[-1,1]^K

source.label: non_asymptotic_lower_bound_corollary

results.notes: Lower bound on the probability of ruin; the authors believe it is not tight.

source.label: exploit_proba_optimality
source.quote: It holds that \exp(- B\sum_{k=1}^K \alpha_k(B) \gamma(F_k)) \leq p^{\mathrm{EX}}(\frac{B}{K}, \dots, \frac{B}{K}) \leq \exp(- B\sum_{k=1}^K (\alpha_k(B) - \frac{1}{B}) \gamma(F_k)).

results.notes: Upper bound on the ruin probability of the generalized EXPLOIT policies. The lower side of the sandwich is not recorded separately.
